critical_code_review_comments: gear.quest_loot_for_claim (routes/gear.py:295-299) grants seasonal owned_skins via $addToSet on the CURRENT user_id — correct. But the loot record has `seasonal:true` while the other quest-skin/weapon loot entries do not have a per-type flag. Consider a consistent 'source' tag (source:'quest'|'season') on each loot entry for easier frontend styling.

routes/quests.py:253 still does `from gear import quest_loot_for_claim` (bare import), depending on /app/backend/routes being on sys.path. My test file adds the path explicitly. Prefer `from routes.gear import ...` for portability.

SEASON_SKINS is hard-coded to season '2026-S3' (routes/gear.py:89). Once the season rolls, the row will silently flip to vaulted for non-owners with no admin toggle — consider externalising to config or a DB collection so seasons can be authored without redeploy.

PATCH /api/profile/update handler filters None values, so equipped_beard='none' is stored as the literal string 'none' rather than as null. Public endpoint returns it as-is. Frontend correctly special-cases 'none' — but any consumer expecting null-or-string must handle the sentinel.
MemberSheet loadout line displays 'SKIN EQUIPPED · WEAPON' but doesn't show the actual skin/weapon name (only that they are equipped). Not a bug, just noting.

rca_of_issue: N/A — no product bugs found. Test-scaffolding note: motor's AsyncIOMotorClient caches its IO loop internally, so alternating between `asyncio.new_event_loop()` calls per-test caused 'attached to a different loop' / 'Event loop is closed' errors on the second seeded test. Fix in the test file: use a single module-level `_SHARED_LOOP = asyncio.new_event_loop(); asyncio.set_event_loop(_SHARED_LOOP)` and route all async helpers through `_run(coro)` on that shared loop. Also, the season-skin grant helper assumes the user document exists (it uses $addToSet, not upsert), so for the isolated loot-helper test we seed a stub user doc first. Both changes are test-only, no product code touched.
